matches.note: Findlay prints it as KINSALE OLD HEAD. Row 367 is the Kinsale Harbour light at Fort Charles, which is a different light.
Findlay's 'Dungarvan' entry is the 'White tower, 44 ft. high, on Ballinacourty Pt.'
The reports print 'Hook Tower' and Findlay prints HOOK POINT. It is the tower on the east side of the entrance to Waterford Harbour, at 52 7.4N 6 55.9W.
Findlay calls it SALTEES LT.-VESSEL. Its description puts it 'In 29 fathoms, off Coningbeg Rock'. It is the only light-vessel between Dungarvan and Barrels Rock.
One report prints 'Tuskar Rock Lt.-ship', which is a slip. Tuskar is a tower on the rock, and Findlay lists no light-vessel there.
The station is part 1 of this row, the white tower. Part 2 is the harbour pier light printed in the same row.
The reports misprint it once as 'Kirk Bank'.
Findlay prints HOWTH-BAILEY. Row 398 is the Howth Harbour pier light, which is a different light.
Findlay says the vessel 'Supersedes S. Rock lt.-ho.'

Findlay's MEW ISLAND entry, established 1884. Before 1884 the light stood on the old Copeland (Lighthouse) Island, which Findlay 1887 no longer lists. For the 1881-1883 reports this row gives the wrong position and character.
Findlay prints both Maidens towers in one row: 'Towers, 76 & 68 ft. high ... 800 yds. apart'.
This is the same row as Maidens North; the pair is printed together.
The tower 'on Altacarry or N.E. point'. It is the only Rathlin light in 1887.
The reports print 'Lough Swilly' and Findlay prints FANNET POINT, the light at the entrance to Lough Swilly. In the lists it sits next to Dunree Head, which is the other Swilly light.
Findlay prints ARANMORE ISLAND. The row includes a lower fixed red light from the same tower.

The reports print only 'Killybegs'. Findlay's row 427, headed 'Killybegs', is the St John Point light (54 34.1N 8 27.6W). Row 428 is Rotten Island, at the harbour entrance (54 36.8N 8 26.4W). I followed your id (Rotten Island), but on the printed name alone row 427 is just as possible.
Findlay's row covers two leading lights ('Two fixed bright lights; in one'). Its longitude is blank.
Findlay prints both Eagle Island towers in one row with one position.
This is the same row as Eagle Island East.
This is the Black Rock off Mayo, at 54 4.2N 10 19.3W, which falls between Eagle Island and Blacksod in coast order. Row 429, also 'Black Rock', is the Sligo harbour light (54 18N 8 37W).
Findlay prints 'Black Sod Quay', described as a 'House on Black Sod Point'.
Findlay prints both Slyne Head towers in one row. The N. light is revolving and the S. light is fixed.
This is the same row as Slyne Head North.
The reports' 'Arran Island N.' is Findlay's EERAGH ISLAND, on the west point of the Aran group.
The reports' 'Arran Island S.' is Findlay's Inisheer Island. One report prints it as 'Straw Island, S.', which is a slip.
Findlay files this under 'Tralee' and describes it as 'On Little Samphire Island'.
Findlay prints TEARAGHT ISLAND.
The Calf Rock lighthouse was destroyed in the gale of 26 Nov 1881; Findlay still prints the entry, marked '(Lighthouse destroyed)'. The 1881 report comes before the destruction.

Dursey Island has no row of its own in Findlay 1887. Row 451 (Calf Rock) says 'A temporary lt. of same character is shown from lt.-ho. on S.W. extr. o[f ...]', and the transcription is cut off at that point. That temporary light is almost certainly on Dursey Island, which replaced Calf Rock in the reports from 1882. The position printed in the row is Calf Rock's, not Dursey's.

notes:
I matched all 47 stations to a Findlay 1887 row; none came out null. Four rows each cover two stations: 413 (Maidens N/S), 433 (Eagle Island E/W), 437 (Slyne Head N/S) and 451 (Calf Rock and Dursey Island). No station needed extra_rows: where Findlay prints a high and low pair, it puts them in one row.

Things to check:
1. Killybegs: the reports print only 'Killybegs'. Findlay row 427 'Killybegs' is St John Point, and row 428 is Rotten Island. I gave row 428 to match your id 'rotten-island'. If the observer was at St John Point, use row 427 instead. The two are about 2.7' apart in latitude.
2. Dursey Island: the transcription of row 451's description stops at 'S.W. extr. o'. Check in the scan that the temporary light is on Dursey Island. The lat/long in that row are Calf Rock's, so Dursey needs its own position.
3. Copeland: Findlay 1887 has only the Mew Island light, established 1884. The 1881-1883 reports were from the old light on Copeland (Lighthouse) Island, which needs a different position and character.
4. Coningbeg L.V.: Findlay names it SALTEES LT.-VESSEL. The match rests on 'off Coningbeg Rock' and the coast order.
5. Blackrock (Mayo): use row 434, not row 429. Row 429 is the Black Rock light at Sligo harbour.
6. Positions missing from Findlay: Oyster Island (row 430) has no longitude. Row 437 (Slyne Head) and row 433 (Eagle Island) each give one position for two towers.
7. Slips in the reports: 'Tuskar Rock Lt.-ship' (Tuskar is a lighthouse), 'Kirk Bank' (for Kish Bank), and 'Straw Island, S.' (for Arran Island S., i.e. Inisheer).
8. Row 416 'Inishowen' prints its latitude as 53 13.6, which must be 55. No station uses this row, but it is a transcription or print error you may want to fix.
